title: Responses API
summary: Responses takes and returns typed Items, can hold state on the server, and adds built-in tools, background runs and encrypted reasoning. OpenAI recommends it for new projects.
useIf: You build new work on OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, use reasoning models with tools, or want built-in tools and server-held state.
avoidIf: You must target many OpenAI-compatible vendors with one format, or a retention policy forbids server-held state and you have not designed a stateless path.

explain.md: `POST /v1/responses` works with **Items**, typed objects such as `message`, `reasoning`, `function_call` and `function_call_output`. The `output` array can hold several items, so never assume the text sits at index 0. System text goes in top-level `instructions`, and `text.format` replaces `response_format`. OpenAI reports, from internal tests, a 3% SWE-bench gain and 40% to 80% better cache use against Chat Completions (vendor claims) [[r6]].

explain.caption: Three ways to carry state
head: Option
How
Retention and cost notes
rows: Send the items each turn, with `store: false` if needed
Works under ZDR. You manage trimming. Keep ordering stable for caching
Responses are stored 30 days. Earlier input tokens bill again. `instructions` are not carried over
Released 2025-08-20. No 30 day TTL. Not ZDR eligible [[r7]] [[r10]]

explain.title: Chaining with previous_response_id
explain.code:
r1 = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-6-sol",
    instructions="Be brief.",
    input="Summarise this ticket: ...",
)
r2 = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-6-sol",
    instructions="Be brief.",  # not carried over, so repeat it
    input="Draft a reply.",
    previous_response_id=r1.id,
)
explain.caption: Billing counts the earlier input tokens again on the second call.

explain.md: **Built-in tools** listed for GPT-6 Astra include `web_search`, `file_search`, `image_generation`, `code_interpreter`, `hosted_shell`, `apply_patch`, `skills`, `computer_use`, `mcp` and `tool_search` [[r1]]. On Azure, remote MCP needs explicit approval by default, Code Interpreter has extra charges and a container holds up to 1,000 files [[r34]].

In **stateless mode** (`store: false`, or a ZDR organisation) reasoning items carry `encrypted_content`. Replay every output item, encrypted reasoning included, so the model keeps its reasoning context [[r3]]. Other parameters include `truncation` (`auto` or `disabled`, default `disabled`, which fails with 400 on overflow), `max_tool_calls`, `background`, `service_tier` and `prompt_cache_key` [[r4]].

explain.title: Store defaults surprise people
explain.md: Responses are stored by default, response objects live 30 days, and `store: false` does not mean nothing is kept: abuse monitoring logs can hold content up to 30 days unless ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring applies [[r10]]. `/v1/conversations` and `/v1/files` are not ZDR eligible.

use: Reasoning with tools on GPT-5.4 and later, GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol
You want fewer lines of state code and can accept server-held history
You use built-in tools or background mode
avoid: Cross-vendor gateways that need one message format
Server state when a no-retention policy applies and you have not planned a stateless replay
flips: ZDR applies: set `store` false, replay items and keep encrypted reasoning
Threads must live for months with audit: use the Conversations API after a retention review
A short chat with low risk: `previous_response_id` is the least code

pitfalls.cause: `output` can start with a reasoning or tool item
pitfalls.fix: Iterate items and pick the `message` item, or use the SDK's output text helper

pitfalls.symptom: The second turn ignores the system prompt
Reasoning context is lost in a ZDR deployment
pitfalls.cause: Encrypted reasoning items were not replayed

pitfalls.symptom: A stored conversation breaks a no-retention policy
pitfalls.cause: The Conversations API is not ZDR eligible
pitfalls.fix: Use stateless replay with `store: false`, or change the policy knowingly

scenarios.title: A ZDR organisation builds a reasoning agent
scenarios.situation: A company with zero data retention builds a multi-turn agent on a reasoning model with tools. Policy forbids storing conversation content with the provider.
unknowns: Is compaction allowed under the policy?
scenarios.question: How do you manage state?

options.name: Use the Conversations API for durable threads
options.why: The Conversations API is not ZDR eligible, so it conflicts with the policy.
options.tradeoff: It suits long-lived threads when no-retention rules do not apply.

options.name: Replay only message and function items and drop the reasoning items
options.why: Simpler to store and it satisfies ZDR.
options.tradeoff: The model loses its reasoning context between turns, so multi-step quality can fall.

options.name: Use `store: false`, keep the history in your own store, and replay every output item including encrypted reasoning
options.why: It satisfies ZDR and keeps the model's reasoning context intact across turns.
options.tradeoff: You manage trimming, ordering for caching and storage security.

flips.then: Add compaction, and check that it works with `store: false`.

scenarios.takeaway: Under ZDR you own the state and must replay encrypted reasoning.

scenarios.title: A short chat widget with low risk
scenarios.situation: A marketing site adds a chat widget. Sessions are about five turns, content is public, and a small team wants the least code.
unknowns: Is a 30 day provider retention acceptable?
Is the cost of re-billed input tokens small?
scenarios.question: Which state approach do you choose?

options.name: `previous_response_id` with `instructions` sent every call
options.why: It is the least code, sessions are short so re-billed input is small, and 30 day retention is acceptable for public content.
options.tradeoff: Earlier input tokens are billed again, and the chain is tied to stored responses.

options.name: Conversations API
options.tradeoff: Adds an object to manage and has no TTL, which is more than a five turn widget needs.

options.name: Replay all items yourself with `store: false`
options.why: More code and state handling for a case with no retention constraint.
options.tradeoff: Right when ZDR applies or you want to control trimming and caching.

flips.if: Sessions grow to hundreds of turns
flips.then: Add compaction or trimming, and consider replaying yourself.
Review retention and move to stateless replay.

scenarios.takeaway: Take the least code that meets the retention rules.

quiz.q: A second call chained with `previous_response_id` ignores the system prompt. What is the cause?
options: `instructions` are not carried over from the previous response
quiz.explain: `previous_response_id` does not carry top-level `instructions`, so send them on each call. Responses live 30 days, not 24 hours.

quiz.q: Which statements about retention are correct?
options: Response objects are kept 30 days by default
The Conversations API is not ZDR eligible
quiz.explain: Responses keep 30 days, Conversations are not ZDR eligible and ZDR forces `store` false. Abuse monitoring logs can keep content up to 30 days unless ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring applies, so `store: false` alone is not a guarantee.

quiz.q: Match the Items to their role.

pairs.r: Text from the user or assistant
Model thinking, replayable as encrypted content when stateless

quiz.explain: These four Items form the core loop of a tool-using conversation in Responses.

flashcards.front: What is an Item in the Responses API?
flashcards.back: A typed object such as `message`, `reasoning`, `function_call` or `function_call_output`. `output` can contain several, so never assume text is at index 0.
They are not carried over. Send them on every call.

flashcards.front: What do you replay in stateless mode?
flashcards.back: Every output item, including reasoning items with `encrypted_content`, so the model keeps its reasoning context.

flashcards.front: Is the Conversations API ZDR eligible?
flashcards.back: No. It was released on 2025-08-20, has no 30 day TTL and conflicts with no-retention policies.
